subject: MediComp pilot: evaluation acceptance tests, exit gates, and close playbook
messages:
From: Lindsay Park <lindsay.park@medicomp.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medicomp.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Evaluation MAP & acceptance criteria for Redwood pilot

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the memory isolation story. Procurement asked me to get a formal mutual action plan (MAP) and a clear set of acceptance tests so we can align legal, security, and engineering for a March go/no-go.

High-level asks from my side:
- A short MAP with milestones and owners (integration -> pilot -> acceptance -> exec signoff).
- Concrete, measurable acceptance tests (latency SLOs, throughput, accuracy/QA pass rates, stability).
- Exit gates and rollback criteria if we see regressions.
- Any required compliance artifacts (SOC2 summary, KMS/HSM details) for our security review.

Can you share a template MAP and acceptance test matrix by EOD Wed? Procurement will also need an estimated SOW value to provision PO (but we can handle that after MAP is agreed).

Appreciate it — Lindsay
Lindsay Park
Sr. Product Manager, Search & AI
MediComp Health

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Lindsay Park <lindsay.park@medicomp.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Request: Evaluation MAP & acceptance criteria for Redwood pilot

Hi Lindsay — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is an initial MAP draft (MediComp_MAP_draft_v0.1.pdf) and a short acceptance test matrix. Summary below so the team has a single view:

Proposed success criteria (measurable):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 350 ms for representative prompts (target 90% of requests meeting p95 SLO during pilot).
- Throughput: sustained 50 concurrent requests / second across the pilot traffic shape (token length distribution attached).
- Quality: average QA pass-rate >= 85% on the agreed prompt set (see eval set A/B/C).
- Stability: no more than 3 service errors (5xx/timeout) per 10k requests over a 72-hour continuous run.
- Data controls: all logs ingested during pilot must be isolated to your VPC and retained per your retention policy (configurable).

Acceptance test matrix (high level):
- Integration smoke (2 business days): auth, routing, KV cache warmup. Exit gate: success = all routes return 200 + valid token stream.
- Pilot run (2 weeks): run eval suites A/B/C daily; compare outputs vs baseline. Exit gate: QA >= 85% and stability metrics within thresholds.
- Security review (parallel): SOC2 summary + KMS details must be submitted and confirmed by your security team. Exit gate: security signoff.
- Exec signoff: product & SRE exec approval after pilot metrics and security cleared.

Rollback policy: automatic fallback to smaller model variant + region failover if p99 latency spikes > 2x baseline for 15m.

Next steps: can we schedule a 45m MAP walkthrough Thur morning? I'll bring Markus and Lauren for implementation and SLO ops.

Attachments: MediComp_MAP_draft_v0.1.pdf (map + matrix)

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: internal: suggested MAP tweaks before sending to customer

Quick internal note — a few small updates I recommend before we send to Lindsay:
- Tighten latency SLO to p95 <= 300ms where possible; mark as stretch target vs required for legal.
- Add a dedicated PII redaction acceptance test in the quality bucket (1k random samples).
- Specify exact duration for the stability run: 72 hours at production replay rate.
- Add canary rollout plan: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with health checks at each step.

If no objections I'll fold these into v1.1.

-Markus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Lindsay Park <lindsay.park@medicomp.com>

Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@medicomp.com>, procurement@medicomp.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 13:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Request: Evaluation MAP & acceptance criteria for Redwood pilot

Thanks Rachel — the draft looks good. A few clarifications from security/procurement:
- Procurement needs a high-level SOW estimate to provision PO (we can do a placeholder).
- Security requests a one-page SOC2 summary and confirmation that we can bring our own KMS/HSM or use Redwood-managed keys; they prefer bring-your-own if possible.
- For acceptance tests please add a PII redaction test as Markus suggested and an SLA degradation behavior test (how system responds when model quality drops).

On timeline: we can aim for an integration week starting Feb 23, pilot the following 2 weeks, and signoff week of Mar 9 — procurement is pushing to close before end of Q1 but can be flexible if security review needs more time.

Could you provide SOC2 summary + KMS options and an updated MAP that includes the PII test and a canary plan?

Lindsay

Hi Lindsay — attached is an updated MAP (MediComp_MAP_v1.1.pdf), a SOC2 summary (SOC2-Summary-Redwood.pdf), and a KMS architecture stub (KMS-architecture-stub.png). Changes included:

- Latency SLO: p95 <= 320ms (required); p95 <= 300ms (stretch). Marked explicitly in the matrix.
- Added PII redaction test: run 1k synthetic PII prompts and verify redaction rate >= 99% (tools & scripts included in the repo).
- Canary plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 30-minute health windows and automatic rollback on >5% error rate increase.
- Stability: 72-hour continuous run at expected replay rate; exit gate = fewer than 3 critical errors per 10k requests.

Proposed MAP milestones (dates are placeholders; please confirm):
- Kickoff & access: Feb 23 (week 1)
- Integration & auth: Feb 23–27
- Pilot run: Mar 1–Mar 14 (2 weeks)
- Acceptance testing: Mar 15–Mar 19
- Exec signoff & SOW finalization: Mar 22–Mar 26

I also added a short section describing the acceptance-test harness (we'll provide the harness and baseline outputs so you can run locally and in your environment).

Action items for you / procurement:
- Confirm whether you prefer Redwood-managed KMS or a BYOK flow (we can share HSM integration docs).
- Provision placeholder PO if procurement wants to lock budget (we can attach SOW to DocuSign).

DocuSign link for the initial SOW (placeholder): https://www.docusign.com/portal/documents/abcdef123456

Attachments: MediComp_MAP_v1.1.pdf, SOC2-Summary-Redwood.pdf, KMS-architecture-stub.png

Best,
